outcome: Presence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in breast milk
cohort: 14 breastfeeding mothers who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 and their newborns
finding: SARS-CoV-2 RNA was detected in the breast milk of one mother, and while four newborns tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 shortly after birth, all infants remained healthy and tested negative for the virus within six weeks, suggesting that breastfeeding by SARS-CoV-2 positive mothers does not increase the risk of infection in their babies.
mod_finding: Only one out of 14 mothers had detectable SARS-CoV-2 RNA in their breast milk, and the infant who was breastfed with this milk did not experience a more severe clinical course compared to the other infants.
